units.content: Identifies candidate bottlenecks preventing capable systems from entering reliable recursive intelligence.

Source pipeline R->G->E->A->C uses local R=representation, G=generator improvement, E=evaluation, A=alignment, C=capability; candidate bottlenecks include representation, generator improvement, evaluation, memory, interface and alignment bandwidth.

content: current AI bottleneck may be reliable self-evaluation
missing-scientist hypothesis: an internal experiment generator may be required
recursive gap separates capability from improvement-of-improvement ability

units.content: Proposes equal-resource comparison of a problem-solving system with one that additionally analyzes and improves its own solving process; compare acceleration.
Bottleneck analysis/hypotheses; no empirical bottleneck localization is reported.
Defines an experiment for detecting whether a system crossed a recursive-intelligence boundary.
Equal-resource fixed-generator vs adaptive-generator design; tracks representation, generator change, reachable frontier, capability, alignment, novel strategies and self-ablation.

content.RA: Delta^2 C_A / Delta^2 C_B recursive advantage

units.content: Predicts fixed/scaling systems can improve C without Delta G_m; adaptive/recursive systems should show Delta G_m>0, reachability expansion and later capability acceleration.
Experiment protocol and expected results only; no experiment execution or observed phase boundary is reported.
Models possible futures of recursively improving intelligence systems.
Distinguishes saturation, stable acceleration and runaway acceleration as possible regimes constrained by budgets/bottlenecks.
A singularity boundary is proposed when generator improvement becomes self-amplifying, including dG_m/dt>0 and R_I>1 under constraints/alignment.
Possible dynamical model; no calibrated singularity forecast or observed runaway regime.
Models intelligence as distributed across humans, AI, interfaces and environments.
Proposes I=f(H,A,I,E), interface-mediated coevolution, system-level generators and the possibility that the unit of intelligence is an agent-interface-environment loop.
Predicts a well-designed human-AI interface can produce greater intelligence velocity/reachability than human or AI components separately; proposes comparative tests.
Coevolution framework/hypothesis; distributed-intelligence advantage is not reported as measured.
Models civilization as a distributed intelligence system with persistent memory, institutions and knowledge generators.
Defines civilization coordinates, external memory, civilization generator G_c, institutions as social computation, interfaces as cognitive infrastructure and coordination/alignment as bottlenecks.
Writing, science, computers and AI are used as interpretive examples of civilization-level memory/generator transitions.
Civilization-scale theory; examples do not establish historical causal claims.
Searches for a substrate-independent invariant across biological, artificial, collective and civilizational intelligence.
Proposes intelligence is not identical to substrate and can be characterized by organization, adaptation, representation, optimization/feedback and generator improvement.
Introduces source-local universal intelligence coordinates/functions such as U=(R,G,F,A) and I_U=f(R,G_m,F,A,B).
Universal-substrate hypothesis; cross-substrate equivalence is not empirically established.
Explores how adaptive intelligence might emerge from non-intelligent physical processes.

Proposes a gradual chain from physical dynamics through self-organization, adaptation, representation, learning and recursive improvement; information gains causal role through feedback, memory and selection.
Autocatalysis, life, genetics, brains, culture and science are used as illustrative stages, not as independently validated lineage evidence.
Origin model/interpretation; not an established account of intelligence origins.
Models the map-territory boundary between reality, observation, internal representation and action.
Useful representation preserves relevant/predictive/causal structure under resource-bounded compression; intelligence acts through models rather than direct access to reality.

Overfitting, ideology, hallucination and scientific representation replacement are used as interpretive examples; 'controlled hallucination' is source rhetoric about useful approximation, not an empirical result.
Representation-boundary theory; no quantified D_RT measurement is reported.
Explores selection among possible representations using invariants, compression, prediction, transfer and causal validity.
Intelligence is framed as search over representation spaces; better coordinate systems collapse many cases into stable structure and reduce search complexity.
Geometry, physics, ML, calculus, Fourier transforms and programming are illustrative coordinate/invariant examples.
Representation-selection theory/proposed score; no validated S(R) estimator is reported.
Explores why useful compression may increase generative/search power.
Proposes intelligent compression removes redundancy while preserving predictive structure; compressed rules/coordinates can increase meaningful generative capacity and search leverage.
Uses MDL-like L(Model)+L(Data|Model), compression frontier, G_m=f(R_q), and conceptual Generative Power proportional to Useful Compression x Search Capacity.
Compression-generation theory/interpretation, not a measured universal proportionality.
Defines how quickly representations/discoveries propagate through adoption and implementation into changes in reality.

content.v_C: Delta Future State / Delta Time causal velocity

units.content: Representation quality and causal velocity are distinct; influence can be limited by transmission/adoption/execution even when knowledge is strong.
Causal-velocity construct/theory; historical examples such as internet protocols are interpretive, not measured v_C records.
Models how influence accumulates into persistent future dependency/irreplaceability.
Proposes reusable representations/generator improvements can create superlinear/persistent causal mass by changing many downstream future paths.
Causal-mass model; examples including mathematics/Einstein/programming languages are illustrative and not source-reported causal estimates.
Attempts a grand unification around intelligence as transformation of reachable future space.

Proposes representation, compression and generator improvement as ways to expand reachability; alignment as trajectory selection; causal mass as persistent reachability change; intelligence as controlled reachability expansion.
Conceptual I=f(Delta R,Delta K,Delta G_m,Delta P^reach,A), plus source definitions of AGI, alignment and civilization in reachability terms.
The frozen file repeats its title, purpose and sections 1-8 before continuing with section 9; repeated content remains a second source occurrence but adds zero warrant independence.
Source calls this the end of the initial framework and a theory of intelligence as adaptive reachability transformation; this self-compression does not supersede earlier source layers.
Intra-file repetition count is preserved as occurrence evidence only; WARRANT_INDEPENDENCE_STATUS=NOT_ESTABLISHED and WARRANT_MULTIPLICITY_EFFECT=NONE.
Reframes alignment around maintained coupling between internal representations and reality.
Defines A as degree of causal model-reality coupling and proposes truth as a maintained correction process rather than static fact storage.

content.A_T: function of representation quality, feedback effectiveness, intervention testing, uncertainty calibration

units.content: Reality detachment, goal/proxy substitution, representation lock-in and false compression are proposed alignment failures.
Truth-alignment hypothesis/theory; equations are conceptual and no measured D_R trajectory is reported.
Converts prior conceptual claims into a proposed falsifiable experimental program.

Proposes equal-resource adaptive-vs-fixed generator tests, representation tests, reachability expansion, generator velocity, acceleration, causal ablation, truth coupling, hallucination resistance, representation replacement, compression and causal-mass tests.
Predicts recursive systems should improve generator quality/reachability/capability while preserving reality/alignment; stronger representations should improve prediction/transfer.

Lists failures such as self-improvement without reachability expansion, acceleration without generator change, representation improvement without prediction improvement and capability gains with declining alignment.
Experimental validation protocol only; no validation run or result is reported.
Translates recursive reachability expansion into a candidate implementable AGI architecture.
Stack includes representation/world model, search, improvement generator, validation/evaluation, truth coupling, alignment, interfaces, memory and tool integration in a recursive loop.
Proposes an AGI phase transition when G_m changes autonomously and architecture begins improving its own architecture under validation.
Representation, evaluation, search and alignment are proposed engineering bottlenecks.
Engineering target/specification; no implemented architecture exists on the frozen R09 tree.
Designs control systems intended to preserve trajectory coherence while reachability/capability expands.

content.G_A: alignment gap C-A and later also alignment improvement generator in a distinct source-local use

units.content: Proposes reality coupling, self-correction/uncertainty, alignment generator, feedback control, proxy-goal verification, representation alignment and interpretability/ablation loops.
Recursive intelligence is proposed to require both improvement-generator growth and adaptive alignment/control growth rather than capability expansion alone.
Alignment engineering proposal; duplicated G_A notation is preserved locally and not reconciled by token identity.
Models civilization as a distributed intelligence system capable of intentionally improving its own discovery/coordination mechanisms.
Defines civilization generator G_c, institutions as search/social computation, cognitive infrastructure, civilization velocity, alignment/coordination and risk under distributed optimizers.
Language, writing, science, computers, AI, education, markets, law and institutions illustrate source interpretations of civilization-level cognitive infrastructure.
Civilization strategy theory; no civilization-level experimental result is reported.
Models possible intelligence systems/trajectories as movement through an evolutionary landscape.
Proposes multidimensional intelligence landscapes, representation/generator frontiers, attractors, exploration-exploitation balance, recursive evolution and civilization as an evolutionary engine.
Introduces L_I, F_I(R,G,A,B), representation/generator frontiers, trajectory/path notation and dG_m/dt as a candidate singularity/landscape-acceleration variable.
Frozen source uses malformed bracket/equation Markdown in multiple places; conceptual content remains substantially recoverable and is not treated as parser failure.
Evolutionary-landscape theory, not an empirically mapped intelligence landscape.
